Links: [{"title":"Row Level Security","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security"},{"title":"Securing your API","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api"},{"title":"Securing your data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/secure-data"},{"title":"RAG with Permissions","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/rag-with-permissions"},{"title":"Database","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview"},{"title":"Tables and data","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/tables"},{"title":"Introducing: Postgres Best Practices","url":"https://supabase.com/blog/postgres-best-practices-for-ai-agents"},{"title":"API keys","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/api-keys"},{"title":"Realtime Authorization","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/authorization"},{"title":"Production Checklist","url":"https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/going-into-prod"}]

The main Supabase RLS guide is at supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security. It has three parts: an explanation of how grants and policies work together, a step-by-step procedure for securing each table, and a reference for helper functions used in policy expressions.

Key points from the results:

- **Grants come first.** Postgres runs two checks before a client touches a table. Grants decide whether a role can run an operation on the table at all. Policies decide which rows that operation applies to.
- **Existing projects may have broad default grants.** On existing projects, a new table in public starts with every privilege already granted to all three roles, and adding policies does not remove those grants.
- **Secure each table in four steps.** Per the guide, you enable RLS and set grants, write a policy per operation, write a test file under supabase/tests/, and run `supabase test db`.
- **Policy examples.** The guide includes sample SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE policies for a `profiles` table keyed on `auth.uid()`, and it recommends indexing columns that policies filter on.
- **Views can bypass RLS.** Views bypass RLS by default because they are usually created with the postgres user. On Postgres 15+, the guide suggests `security_invoker = true`.
- **Keys and roles.** Publishable keys resolve to the `anon` or `authenticated` role, while secret keys use `service_role`, which bypasses RLS (per the API keys page).

The Securing your API page and the Tables and data page cover the same topics from the Data API and table-creation angles. Note that these pages may describe newer key formats and default behaviors than older Supabase material you may have seen.
